title: What if a war started out of nowhere?
fact_source: Hawaii false ballistic missile alert, 13 Jan 2018 – correction sent 38 minutes later (ABC7 'Timeline of trepidation: 38 minutes of fear in Hawaii'; PBS NewsHour; FCC report). Shelter advice: Ready.gov nuclear explosion guidance – get inside, basement or middle of the building.

lines.text: What if a war started out of nowhere?
You're standing at a busy crossing in Manhattan. It's a normal Tuesday afternoon.
Taxis honk. People rush past you. Your coffee is still hot.
And then, every phone around you screams at the exact same moment.
Emergency alert. Missile threat inbound. Seek immediate shelter. This is not a drill.
For one second, nobody moves. Everyone just stares at their screen.
Then the sirens start, and the whole street breaks into a run.
The official advice is simple. Get inside. Go to the basement, or the middle of a building.
So you grab the hand of a stranger, and pull her down into the subway.
Down here, hundreds of people sit in silence, refreshing the news. Nothing comes.
Thirty eight minutes later, a second message arrives.
False alarm. Someone pressed the wrong button.
This really happened. In Hawaii, in 2018, a whole state believed for thirty eight minutes that war had begun.
